When SpaceX isn't catching rockets, it's signing deals with AI companies. In February, the company behind Starlink merged with xAI, which includes Twitter (now renamed X). In April, SpaceX reached an agreement with Cursor—a competitor to Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex. As of August 14, the acquisition has been completed. SpaceXAI (its new name) recently also launched Grok Bot and the Grok 4.6 model with Cursor's assistance.

Update (August 14, 2026): SpaceXAI has completed its acquisition of Cursor.

Update (June 16, 2026): SpaceX acquired Cursor a week after becoming a publicly listed company.

Below is the original updated version:

SpaceX struck a $10 billion deal with Cursor before its $60 billion acquisition

Cursor has long been popular among software engineers who use Macs to write AI programs. It was one of the earliest services to connect large language model AI to the application development process.

The two companies said SpaceX and Cursor were "working closely together in April, committed to creating the world's best AI for coding and knowledge work."

The original collaboration included SpaceX paying Cursor $1 billion:

Cursor disclosed further details of the collaboration before its acquisition on April today:

Cursor is partnering with SpaceX to accelerate our model training work. Composer was our first agentic coding model, launched less than six months ago. Composer 1.5 then scaled up reinforcement learning by more than 20 times. After that, Composer 2 added continual pre-training, achieving frontier-level performance at a cost far lower than other models. Every increase in computing power translates into significant gains in model capability. We have always wanted to push our training work further, but have been constrained by computing power. Through this partnership, our team will leverage xAI's Colossus infrastructure to dramatically enhance the intelligence of our models.

The SpaceX-Cursor partnership strengthens a competitor to the agentic coding software from Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex.
